title: How Are You Feeling Today?
paragraphs: Kamila Seitkali writes a blog for WKU students. Every week she posts a short article about student life. This week, her topic is feelings.

'How are you feeling today?' she begins. 'Most of us answer: Fine, thanks. But is that the truth? University life brings many emotions — excitement, stress, joy, loneliness, pride, and confusion. All of these are normal.'

Kamila describes her own experience. 'I remember my first week at WKU. I felt excited about my new life, but I also felt overwhelmed. There were new people, new rules, new subjects. I didn't know what to feel first.'

'The turning point came when I started talking,' she writes. 'I told my friend Zhibek that I was feeling anxious about my first English test. She listened. She didn't judge me. She just said: Me too. And suddenly, I felt much better.'

Research shows that naming your feelings is powerful. When you say 'I feel stressed' instead of just feeling it, the emotion becomes smaller. Psychologists call this 'labelling' your emotions. It helps you think more clearly.
Kamila ends her article with a question: 'What emotion are you avoiding right now? Name it. Write it down. Talk to a friend. You might be surprised how much better you feel afterwards.'

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I love doing presentations eventually, but I hate preparing them. Funny, right?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's actually really helpful to know. I feel better already.
